# img snapshot

Repository: https://github.com/joshuarli/img
Base: 3213d3c81481fb0f3873f0f4c20e952ea108df91
Branch: master (pushed 2026-11-25, 2026-11-26 and 2026-11-26 for the JPEG encoder; the PNG commits are cd28108 and its two parents, rebased onto master 137ad9e, the JPEG decoder is 7c3034e with its standards follow-up f2cf102, and the JPEG encoder is c9ec6ab with its standards follow-up 6867940. The GIF commits start at 8878365 and end at 8bdf3d7, pushed 2026-11-27.)
Commit: 686794007482c8fbecd413c9f8492c2b591d0a08 for `codecs/png` and `codecs/jpeg`; 8bdf3d71a240f8b2b63d46d7326879b918970992 for `codecs/gif`. The snapshot crates are byte-identical to those directories at their respective commits.
Patch: five local commits on the base give the native codecs (jpegli, libjpeg-turbo, dav1d, libavif) a default-on `native-codecs` feature and add `codecs/png`, the streaming PNG codec exported as `img::png_stream`; Chromium's rust_png_ffi reader and writer options and transformations, `next_interlaced_row`, `next_frame_info`, the Adam7 expand and splat helpers, and the Level1WithUpFilter, Fastest, Fast, Balanced and High encoder levels in `png_stream::chromium`; `codecs/jpeg`, the pure-Rust libjpeg-turbo-exact streaming decoder exported as `img::jpeg_stream` with Chromium's header, orientation, density and ICC metadata behavior and a suspending source; and `codecs/jpeg`'s baseline encoder, exported as `img_jpeg::encode_stream` with `EncodeColorSpace`, `Downsample`, `EncodeOptions` and `EncodeError`: the libjpeg-turbo 3.1.0 YCbCr tables, h2v1/h2v2 downsampling, islow integer FDCT, reciprocal quantization, optimal Huffman tables and entropy writer, all as reusable mechanisms; the Chromium canvas policy (quality to downsampling, blend-on-black and the sRGB ICC segment) stays in `crates/jpeg-encode`.

Ten further commits add `codecs/gif`, a pure-Rust Wuffs-compatible GIF stream decoder exported as `img_gif`: 8878365 introduces the decoder; 5a1b547 keeps a zero loop count infinite; 6c6c600 ignores local build artifacts; d18ab64 matches Wuffs' LZW code space and frame config; 596259e follows Wuffs' deferred LZW code width; fc0ae54 tracks the Wuffs save code for code-width growth and the KwKwK case; 8ec7157 aligns the save code with Wuffs v0.3; c6a9f77 expands the canvas to the first frame bounds; f708489 paints LZW output before reporting bad codes; 490a577 matches Wuffs frame bounds and canvas edge cases (zero-area frames, raw row width for clipped frames, invalid literal widths and empty canvases); 26f5bb8 measures required pixels against the raw frame extent so truncated frames stay partial; and 8bdf3d7 corrects the test expectation for a clipped zero-width frame. Frame dependency, required-frame, repetition and N32 policy stay in `crates/gif`.

The snapshot contains the `img-png`, `img-jpeg` and `img-gif` package sources (`codecs/png`, `codecs/jpeg` and `codecs/gif`) and the img licenses. All three packages are pure Rust with no `-sys` or C dependency: `img-png` depends on the pinned png crate 0.18.1 used by Chromium, while `img-jpeg` and `img-gif` have no external dependency.
